<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="אדר_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518917334_theRebbe_880" batchId="meluket-_D7_90_D7_93_D7_A8_meluket__BH_POST_1766518917334_theRebbe_880__p007">
  <section v="18">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Based on this, the statement in the maamar that through Israel adding to the level of Moshe the lamp becomes perpetual is explained, for the revelation of the essence of the soul through Moshe is constant, yet there is a distinction between evening and morning in how this essence is revealed.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And based on this, one can understand what is said in the maamar,</t>
    <t s="1">that through Israel adding</t>
    <t s="2">(through their service)</t>
    <t s="3">to the level of Moshe,</t>
    <t s="4">through this there will be a perpetual lamp,</t>
    <t s="5">for seemingly,</t>
    <t s="6">that the lamp of the soul</t>
    <t s="7">(the lamp</t>
    <t s="8">of G-d is the soul of man)</t>
    <t s="9">is perpetual</t>
    <t s="10">(equally,</t>
    <t s="11">without change),</t>
    <t s="12">is through the revelation of the essence of the soul drawn by Moshe</t>
    <t s="13">(and you shall command),</t>
    <t s="14">for in the essence of the soul, change does not apply,</t>
    <t s="15">and in the maamar it says that the matter of a perpetual lamp is through Israel adding to the level of Moshe,</t>
    <t s="16">"and they shall take to you."</t>
    <t s="17">And one could say,</t>
    <t s="18">that in the revelation of the essence of the soul in a top-down manner through "and you shall command,"</t>
    <t s="19">there is a distinction between evening and morning.</t>
    <t s="20">For the primary revelation of it is when there are concealments and veils</t>
    <t s="21">(evening)</t>
    <t s="22">through which the power of self-sacrifice is aroused and revealed,</t>
    <t s="23">as explained above</t>
    <t s="24">(section ten),</t>
    <t s="25">that even those who during the time of the decree</t>
    <t s="26">(evening)</t>
    <t s="27">stood with self-sacrifice,</t>
    <t s="28">when they came to a place where it was possible to engage in Torah and mitzvos with ease</t>
    <t s="29">(morning),</t>
    <t s="30">the self-sacrifice they had previously is not apparent in them.</t>
    <t s="31">And the true matter of a perpetual lamp</t>
    <t s="32">(in which change does not apply)</t>
    <t s="33">is through the service of Israel that even the revealed powers become one with the essence of the soul,</t>
    <t s="34">"and they shall take to you."</t>
  </section>
  <section v="19">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Based on this, the verse "crushed for the light" following "and they shall take to you" is explained, for it includes Israel being crushed and broken by exile, which through their service aligns their revealed powers with the essence of the soul, revealing the soul's light rooted in Atzmus.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And based on this, one can explain that "crushed for the light" is stated in the verse in continuation of "and they shall take to you," etc.,</t>
    <t s="1">for in "crushed for the light" is also included that Israel are broken and crushed</t>
    <t s="2">(crushed)</t>
    <t s="3">from being in exile,</t>
    <t s="4">for this matter is through the service of Israel that even their revealed powers become aligned with the essence of the soul,</t>
    <t s="5">and the aspect of the light of the soul revealed through this is the essence of the soul as it is rooted in Atzmus,</t>
    <t s="6">and therefore "crushed for the light" is stated in continuation of "and they shall take to you," etc.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="20">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The simple explanation of "and you shall command the children of Israel, and they shall take to you" is that Moshe commands Israel, and from this it is understood that Moshe empowers them for their own service, and similarly the Moshe of our generation, the Rebbe, arouses faith so that they serve with their own power, achieving a perpetual lamp without change.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">10)</t>
    <t s="1">B)</t>
    <t s="2">And behold, the explanation</t>
    <t s="3">(in simple terms)</t>
    <t s="4">of "and you shall command the children of Israel, and they shall take to you," etc., is that Moshe will command the children of Israel that they shall take to you, etc.</t>
    <t s="5">And from this it is also understood in the inner meaning of the matters,</t>
    <t s="6">that this that Moshe commands and connects the children of Israel is in a manner that he draws down for them the granting of power also for "and they shall take to you," etc.</t>
    <t s="7">And likewise is it regarding the Moshe of our generation,</t>
    <t s="8">His Holiness, my master, my father-in-law, the Rebbe, the Nasi of our generation,</t>
    <t s="9">that his service to arouse and reveal the faith that is in every Jew from the aspect of the essence of the soul is in a manner that afterwards they will serve with their own power,</t>
    <t s="10">to the point that they will be a perpetual lamp in which change does not apply even from the aspect of the revealed powers.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
